sections.h2: Where is Palm Springs, Florida, and what is the village like?
sections.html:
This Palm Springs is a village in central Palm Beach County, not the California desert city. It was chartered by the 1957 legislature on about 700 acres of pastureland with a dairy barn and no residents.

By August 1958 the first section opened with some 800 homes on paved, landscaped streets. The village says it now has about 28,000 residents, a mix of single-family homes, townhomes, apartments and condominiums, and that two-thirds of homes were single-family by 1997.

That mix matters when you sell. A 1960s ranch, a townhouse and a condo each sell to a different buyer, and condo or townhome sellers should also line up association paperwork early.

sections.h2: What are the village's boundaries and main corridors?
sections.html:
The village describes Congress Avenue running south to Lake Worth Road, west to Military Trail and north along the east side of Military Trail to Forest Hill Boulevard. It extends east toward Florida Mango Road and south along it to 10th Avenue North.

  • Congress Avenue and Lake Worth Road anchor commercial areas.
  • Palm Springs Elementary opened in 1959, Palm Springs Middle in 1962 and John I. Leonard High School in 1965.
  • A Community Redevelopment Agency works on older commercial areas, streetscapes and walkability.

Redevelopment along these corridors is a selling point for some buyers. Ask the village what projects are planned near your street.

sections.h2: How do Palm Beach County property taxes apply to a Palm Springs house?
sections.html:
Palm Beach County officials follow the statewide schedule: valuation on January 1, then bills in November.

Florida property tax dates that apply in Palm Springs
DateEvent
January 1Assessment date
March 1Exemption filing deadline
AugustProposed tax (TRIM) notice mailed
NovemberTax bills sent, 4 percent discount for payment that month
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

Disagree with value? A petition goes to the clerk within 25 days of the TRIM notice. Ask the county appraiser about your parcel and exemptions.

sections.h2: How much does homestead protect a Palm Springs owner?
sections.html:
A permanent residence can carry up to $50,000 of exemption, claimed on Form DR-501 by March 1. Save Our Homes limits yearly assessed growth to the smaller of 3 percent or CPI, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.

Once you sell, the new owner starts at just value. Long-time owners are often surprised that a buyer's tax bill can be far higher than theirs. Ask a lender or agent to run the buyer's likely bill rather than quoting yours.

sections.h2: Which charges apply when the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Outside Miami-Dade, the state revenue agency lists deed stamp tax at 70 cents per $100. The statute says consideration includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property.

  • Clerk recording starts at $5.00 for page one, then $4.00 for each additional page.
  • A $1.00 charge applies for each name beyond four.
  • Extra modernization and technology charges apply per page.

Your closing agent will total these. Estate planning transfers have no special stamp exemption according to the state.

sections.h2: Should I make repairs or check permits first?
sections.html:
Houses built in the late 1950s and 1960s may need roofs, wiring, plumbing or windows updated before an insurer or lender is comfortable. An investor may absorb that risk, while a financed buyer may ask you to fix it first.

Ask the village building office about permits from earlier work. Keep invoices and inspection records, since unclosed permits tend to surface during title review.

sections.h2: What should a Palm Springs owner know about tax certificates and tax deeds?
sections.html:
Delinquency starts April 1, with certificate sales by June 1. For two years after April 1 of the issue year the certificate buyer cannot demand payment from the owner, and a tax deed application costs $75.

The clerk conducts the auction. A winning bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit, the larger of $200 or 5 percent, and pays in full within a day, not counting weekends and holidays. Selling the house first ends that risk.

  • Homestead property with under $250 delinquent goes to the county instead of auction.
  • Tax deed notice goes to the titleholder, mortgagees and contract for deed buyers.

sections.h2: Who might be living in or claiming a vacant Palm Springs house?
sections.html:
An owner may swear out a complaint asking the sheriff to remove unlawful occupants when no tenancy exists, the occupants are not family and no case is pending. A false statement exposes the owner to damages, including triple the fair market rent.

Adverse possession needs seven years of continued possession and payment of taxes, and occupying a home on that basis before filing the required return is trespass. Vacant house owners should inspect and secure the property often.

sections.h2: How do landlords and tenants handle a sale in Palm Springs?
sections.html:
A landlord's notice can be mailed, handed over, e-mailed under the statute, or left at the unit when the tenant is away, and a lease cannot waive these rules.

Once a court rules for the landlord, a sheriff posts a 24 hour notice before returning possession. A tenant raising defenses other than payment must deposit rent with the court within 5 days or lose them.

sections.h2: What is the village's government like for a seller?
sections.html:
Early village hall services were built to house the clerk, building official and police, and a bond referendum in 1999 funded a new municipal campus completed in 2003. The village says its council focuses on neighborhood character, CRA redevelopment and infrastructure.

Contact the Village of Palm Springs for questions about permits, code compliance and rental rules on your street.

sections.h2: What steps does a Palm Springs seller follow from offer to closing?
sections.html:
A land deed must be written and signed with two witnesses, which your title agent arranges along with recording. Before then, you compare offers and choose a buyer.

  • Confirm who pays doc stamps and recording in the contract.
  • Request a payoff letter if a mortgage exists.
  • Check the tax roll for liens and exemption status.
  • Walk through the house with the buyer's inspector if one is used.

The village's original footprint was 1.6 square miles, so nearby sales are easy for buyers to compare.

sections.h2: Which village landmarks do buyers mention in Palm Springs?
sections.html:
Village Hall was dedicated in February 1960 as an air-conditioned community building, and a 1999 bond vote paid for a new two-story municipal campus finished in July 2003. The campus now includes a water park, playgrounds and a covered pavilion.

Faith communities, scout groups and a garden club formed early, and the village describes itself as a place where children grow up and move next door. Schools opened in 1959, 1962 and 1965. If your house is near the campus or a school, say so in your marketing, and let the buyer verify attendance zones.

sections.h2: Which special situations come up for Palm Springs sellers?
sections.html:
Inherited homes, tenant occupied homes and houses behind on payments all have fixed state rules. Estates under $150,000 non-exempt can use summary administration, unpaid rent starts with a 3 day notice, and foreclosure auctions follow judgments by 20 to 35 days.

If a tenant rents month to month, ending it takes 30 days' notice, and any lease that stays will affect what buyers offer.

faqs.q: Is Palm Springs, FL the same as the California city?
faqs.a: No. It is a village in Palm Beach County chartered in 1957, with about 28,000 residents according to the village.

faqs.q: When do Palm Beach County tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: In November, under the state calendar. Taxes unpaid after the year turns become delinquent on April 1.

faqs.q: Is there a state tax on the deed in Palm Springs?
faqs.a: Yes. Documentary stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk at recording.
Yes. Petition the clerk within 25 days of the TRIM notice, which arrives in August.

faqs.q: What if my condo has association approval rules?
faqs.a: Request the association's sale rules early, because approval timing can move the closing date.
